title: The goal map: company goals, areas of focus, milestones and features in one view
subtitle: Mock-ups for Simple. Invented data: three goals, four areas (five in the hard case), milestones with 7 days of proof, features with expected and measured lift.

decisions.name: How Simple shows the goal map
decisions.question: How should Simple show and edit company goals, areas of focus, milestones and the features serving them?
decisions.common: A new Simple page, Goal map, in the rail after Roadmap with its own target icon, in Simple's design (light rail, cards, 18 px body). Every proposal shows the goals with today's reading against the target and their status; the guardrail (customer complaints = 0) that every milestone must hold; each milestone's reading, threshold, status (met, on track, at risk, missed, not measured yet) and its 7 days of proof with who confirmed; each feature's expected lift and confidence and, once out, its measured lift (helping, not helping, not measured yet). Every proposal lets the owner add an area, reorder areas (the order holds in every view), edit a goal (its history kept), propose a milestone, attach a feature to a milestone and start a New PRD from a picked milestone and areas, from the same forms. A feature that serves two milestones is drawn once; the other place shows a small note pointing to its card. Every frame's PNG is the first screen; a -full.png beside it shows the whole page and a -dark.png the first screen in dark.

proposals.name: Ladder by area lanes
proposals.what: The three goals sit on top as cards joined by arrows (sign-ups → paid conversions → revenue), each with today's reading against its target, a bar, its status and the math it builds on. Under them a green guardrail strip (customer complaints = 0) that every milestone must hold. Then one grid: the areas are rows in the owner's order (move up or down, add an area), the milestones are columns in steps from left to right, each gate with its reading against its threshold, its status and the last 7 days as proof with who confirmed it. Each feature is a card in the cell of its area under the milestone it serves, with its expected lift and, once out, what it measured (helping, not helping, not measured yet). Propose a milestone and New PRD sit at the top; Edit sits on each goal; Attach a feature sits in each cell a milestone touches.
proposals.why: It is the only proposal where the owner's whole model is drawn at once, in their own shape: what builds on what reads left to right, the area order is the row order every view keeps, a milestone that cuts across areas spans their rows, and a feature that does not help is a red card in the exact place it was meant to help. Every edit happens where the thing sits.
proposals.plus: What builds on what, the area order and which features help read in one look; proof sits on each gate; a proposed milestone appears in place, dashed, until approved.
proposals.cost: Wide: at 1440 only 3 of 7 steps show at a time and the grid scrolls sideways (12 steps in the hard case, still 3 at a time); the hard case page is about 4 screens tall; on a phone the grid becomes a list of milestones with their areas, so the lanes are lost there.

frames.caption: Simple › Goal map. At rest: the three goals with readings against targets, the guardrail strip, and milestones by area: 3 steps show at a time, each with its 7 days of proof, and a line says to scroll sideways for the rest.
The owner clicks Propose a milestone: the form asks for a name, the goal it moves, the threshold, the areas it pulls and what it comes after.

Result after Propose: a dashed column, 40 sign-ups per rep, marked Proposed at step 2 just before 50 sign-ups per rep, with today's 7 days already read; a note at the bottom says it was sent to Dana Whitlock to approve.

Hard case at 1440: 5 areas, 12 milestones, 40 features, revenue not measured yet. 3 of 12 steps show; Guided first week's second place is a small note pointing to its card. The whole page (area 5, More reps, at the bottom) is in the -full PNG.
The same hard case, scrolled down to the steps and sideways to step 3: 8 paid conversions per rep is the red Missed gate, due Oct 31, held 0 of 7 days. The area names stay pinned on the left.
The same hard case at 1512, the owner's window: the same 3 steps at a time, each a little wider.
Phone 390: goals stack with arrows turned down, then the milestones one by one with their proof, areas and features; the lanes grid is not shown on a phone.

proposals.name: Goal tree
proposals.what: One card per goal, in the order they build on each other, with its reading against the target, its status and Edit. Inside each goal its milestones in steps, each with its reading, status, 7 days of proof, the areas it pulls (as numbered chips in the owner's order) and what it comes after; inside each milestone the features serving it with expected and measured lift and Attach a feature. The guardrail strip and an ordered bar of areas (move left or right, add an area) sit on top.
proposals.plus: Reads like a document, top to bottom, with no sideways scroll; works the same on a phone; the goal's own history shows right under it after an edit.
proposals.cost: Areas are only chips, not a structure: you cannot see an area's whole load at a glance. The hard case runs to almost 7 screens, and a milestone that needs one under another goal only says so in words. A shared feature's second place is only a pointer, so the goal you read may not hold the card.

frames.caption: Simple › Goal map. At rest: guardrail, areas in order, then goal 1 with its milestones and their features, indented.
The owner clicks Edit on Paid conversions per rep per day: it says now 5.6, target 10, an empty New target field, and the goal's history (set at 10 on Oct 2).
Typing 12: a note says its 3 milestones keep their thresholds and the highest, 10 paid conversions per rep, would now stop short of the goal.
Result after Save goal: the goal reads ≥ 12, Now 5.6 of 12, its line says Last change: Target 10 → 12, Nov 3, and a note says revenue still aims at $20k: 10 reps × 12 × $167 a conversion.
Hard case at 1440: 5 areas, 12 milestones, 40 features; the page runs to about 7 screens.
The same hard case at 1512: the cards keep the same width, so the page is the same length; only the margins grow.
Phone 390: the same tree, stacked; the 7 proof squares wrap onto a second row where the readings are wide ($10.4k).

proposals.name: Driver tree
proposals.what: The goals' math drawn as boxes: Revenue per day on top, equal to Reps live × Paid conversions per rep × Value of a conversion; under paid conversions, Sign-ups per rep × Conversion rate. Each goal box has its reading, target, status and Edit; each lever box lists the areas pulling it, the milestones it moves with their reading, status and 7 days of proof (and who confirmed it), and the features pulling it with expected and measured lift and the milestones each serves. The guardrail box sits under the tree with the features that keep it. The areas order bar sits on top.
proposals.plus: Shows why each goal moves: which lever is short (conversion rate 18% against 15–25%, value $200) and what pulls it; a new lever is easy to see when empty.
proposals.cost: Milestones are grouped by what they move, not in order, so what builds on what in time is lost; a milestone moved by two boxes shows in both; only 6 features show per box (and N more); boxes run long with the proof inside; the tree changes shape if the math changes.

frames.caption: Simple › Goal map. At rest: revenue = reps × paid conversions per rep × value; paid conversions = sign-ups per rep × conversion rate; each box with its milestones and features.
The owner clicks + Attach a feature: pick a milestone and search the features.
Mid-way: milestone 10 paid conversions per rep, search “trial”, Trial reminder texts (a conversion rate feature that helps today) picked.
Result after Attach: the page scrolls to Conversion rate; Trial reminder texts now serves 10 paid conversions per rep (new), and that milestone reads 2 features here (1 new).
Hard case at 1440: 5 areas, 12 milestones, 40 features. 9 reps live (its milestone reads 9 of 12), revenue and value not measured yet, and 8 paid conversions per rep missed under Conversion rate.
The same hard case at 1512: boxes a little wider, same shape; status chips wrap under the box name when they do not fit.
Phone 390: reps live × paid conversions × value, top to bottom, all full width; under paid conversions, indented, sign-ups × conversion rate.

proposals.name: Scoreboard with drill-in
proposals.what: Big tiles for the three goals and the guardrail, the areas order bar, then one table of milestones sorted by area order: reading against threshold, status, and how many features serve it (helping, not helping). Clicking a row opens a side panel with the milestone's proof (7 days and who confirmed), what it comes after, its features with expected and measured lift, Attach a feature and New PRD from this milestone.
proposals.plus: Shortest page by far (1.6 screens in the hard case); the numbers are big and quick to scan; good for a daily check.
proposals.cost: What builds on what is only words inside the panel; areas are a line of text under each row; one milestone's proof at a time.

frames.caption: Simple › Goal map. At rest: goal tiles and the guardrail tile, areas in order, and the milestones table.
The owner opened 6 paid conversions per rep and clicked New PRD from this milestone: the milestone is picked, areas still to choose.
Mid-way: Customer safety and Conversions picked; a note says the PRD starts with the measure, threshold, guardrail and the 4 features serving it.
Result after Start the PRD: a card says New PRD started for 6 paid conversions per rep, with Open the draft.
Hard case at 1440: 12 milestones in one table, area names wrapping in full; the missed 8 paid conversions per rep is open with its 7 days and Due Oct 31.
The same hard case at 1512: the table and the panel side by side.
Phone 390: each row keeps its reading and features count; the milestone sheet slides up over the dimmed page, which stays still behind it.
